result.area: Institutions tier — invitation, activation, and the authorization boundary an invited account crosses (security engineering)
result.recommendation: Build the invitation as our own object with our own token, and let Supabase Auth do only what it is good at (bcrypt password storage, refresh-token rotation with reuse detection). Do NOT use `supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail()`: I read the source at github.com/supabase/auth and its emailed secret is a `MAILER_OTP_LENGTH`-digit OTP whose stored form is `sha256.Sum224(email + otp)` (`internal/crypto/crypto.go`), and `/verify` accepts exactly that stored string as `token_hash` (`internal/api/verify.go`) — so the database column IS the bearer credential, replayable from any backup or dump, and the underlying secret is ~20 bits. Its invite handler also returns `ErrorCodeEmailExists` for confirmed users (`internal/api/invite.go`), which both leaks existence and breaks our single most common case: a teacher who already has a personal Pro account being invited by her school. Instead: an `org_invitations` row with a 16-byte `selector` (looked up, indexed) plus a 32-byte `verifier` stored only as SHA-256, the verifier carried in the URL *fragment* so it never reaches a server log or a Referer header, single-use, 7-day expiry, rotated on every resend, and consumed only by a POST that carries the new password — never by a GET, because Microsoft Defender Safe Links, Proofpoint and Mimecast pre-click every link in school mail and would otherwise burn the token before the teacher touches it (this exact breakage is supabase/auth issue #1214). Passwords follow ASVS 5.0 §6.2.1/6.2.5/6.2.9 and NIST SP 800-63B-4: 15-character minimum, zero composition rules, NFKC normalisation, HIBP k-anonymity checked by us rather than by Supabase's paid leaked-password feature — with one honest non-conformance recorded, that supabase/auth hard-caps passwords at 72 bytes (`internal/api/password.go`, bcrypt limit), which for two-byte Arabic letters means 36 characters, not the 64 that ASVS 6.2.9 asks for. And on the tension: the zero-gates rule is scoped to the consumer product and survives intact, because an institution is not the same app with extra buttons — it is a second human with power over your account. Everything in this design exists only because someone can now invite, revoke, allocate quota and (with disclosure) read another teacher's results. The scanner is the least interesting difference; the trust model is the real one. To keep decision 1 literally true I recommend the PDF-batch grading path (finding 36) stay ungated in the free tier — the free teacher who scans a stack on the school copier into a PDF must still be able to grade it. What institutions buy is the driver-attached hardware path (TWAIN 2.5 / WIA on Windows, ImageCaptureCore on macOS, SANE on Linux, via a desktop helper), which needs deployment, per-seat licensing and an administrator. Gate the driver, never the file format.

decisions.decision: Own invitation token in our own `org_invitations` table; Supabase Auth is entered only at redemption, server-side, via `auth.admin.createUser({ email, password, email_confirm: true })` inside an Edge Function holding the service_role key, followed immediately by `signInWithPassword`.
decisions.rationale: Verified in supabase/auth source (searched and fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master, 2026-08-14): `GenerateTokenHash = sha256.Sum224(emailOrPhone+otp)`, written to `users.confirmation_token` and `one_time_tokens`, and `verify.go` recomputes/compares that same value as `token_hash`. The stored value is directly replayable, and the seed secret is an OTP of `MAILER_OTP_LENGTH` digits (~20 bits at the default 6). Also, invite link lifetime is governed by the single project-wide Email OTP expiration knob shared with magic links and password recovery, so we cannot give invitations 7 days while keeping recovery at 1 hour. And we need an invitation to be a first-class object with status, quota allocation, inviter, audit trail and supersede semantics — GoTrue has no such object.
decisions.alternativeRejected: `supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email, { data: { org_id } })`, one line of code. Rejected for the replayable stored token, the shared expiry knob, the `email_exists` 422 that dead-ends the already-registered teacher, and because the `data` field lands in `user_metadata`, which the end user can rewrite themselves via PUT /user (verified in internal/api/user.go: `params.Data` is applied for any user; only `app_metadata` is gated by `isAdmin`) — an org_id there is self-service escalation into another school's data.

decisions.decision: Token = selector + verifier. `selector` = 16 bytes (128 bits) from crypto.randomBytes, base64url (22 chars), stored in the clear and uniquely indexed. `verifier` = 32 bytes (256 bits), base64url (43 chars), stored ONLY as `sha256(verifier)` in `verifier_hash bytea`, compared with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Link shape: `https://app.<domain>/ar/invite/<selector>#<verifier>`.
decisions.rationale: The selector gives an indexed O(1) lookup with no scan over hashes and no timing side channel on lookup; the verifier gives 256 bits of unguessable secret whose leak from a database read is useless. SHA-256 rather than bcrypt/argon2 is correct here precisely because the verifier is uniform random — there is no dictionary to attack, and a slow hash would only add latency. Putting the verifier after the `#` keeps it out of the server access log, out of the Referer header on any outbound link from the landing page, and out of any CDN or WAF request log; the page reads `location.hash` and POSTs it. ASVS 5.0 §6.5.4 sets a 20-bit floor for out-of-band codes *that are rate limited*; our link is reachable for 7 days without an interactive rate limiter in front of the secret, so we buy margin instead of relying on throttling.
decisions.alternativeRejected: A single opaque token in the query string, looked up by hashing the whole token (the common pattern). Rejected because the token then appears in access logs, proxy logs and the ESP's click-tracking record, and because hash-only lookup either forces an index on the hash of a value we must not store in a reversible form anyway (fine) or a table scan (not fine at 200-seat orgs × resends).

decisions.decision: Consumption happens only on `POST /invite/:selector/accept` carrying the verifier and the chosen password. `GET /invite/:selector` and `HEAD` are strictly side-effect-free, return 200, and mark nothing used or seen.
decisions.rationale: School mail in Saudi Arabia is overwhelmingly Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace for Education; Defender Safe Links, Proofpoint and Mimecast fetch every URL in an inbound message before the human sees it. Verified this is a live, unresolved failure mode for the platform we sit on: supabase/auth issue #1214 'Magic Links are invalidated by corporate link scanning software'. Requiring a password field submission makes the anti-prefetch interaction the same act as the activation, so we pay no extra UX step. This also satisfies ASVS 5.0 §6.4.1 (activation codes expire after a short period OR on first use) without the classic own-goal of 'first use' being a robot.
decisions.alternativeRejected: User-Agent or IP allowlisting of scanners (they spoof browser UAs and run on cloud IPs shared with real users), and 'respond to HEAD without consuming' alone (Safe Links issues GETs, not HEADs).

decisions.decision: Lifetime 7 days (168h) from creation, hard maximum 14, admin-settable down to 24h. Single use. Resend rotates: the old row goes to `status='superseded'` with `superseded_by` set and a brand-new selector/verifier is generated and mailed. The same secret is never re-sent.
decisions.rationale: Seven days is one Saudi school week plus the Friday–Saturday weekend: an administrator who invites 30 teachers on Sunday morning must not have half of them dead on Tuesday, and lengthening it further only widens the window on a secret sitting in an ESP's logs. Rotation on resend means a leaked or scanned-and-cached first link stops working the moment the admin clicks 'resend', which is the exact moment a confused teacher generates support pressure.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Re-sending the same token (what most 'resend invite' buttons do): it makes the secret's exposure additive across every mailbox, forward and ESP the mail ever touched, and it makes 'the link stopped working' undiagnosable.

decisions.decision: An email that already has a TransferChecker account is attached as a membership, never a second account and never a merge. Redemption for that person is: sign in with your existing password, then the accept POST inserts the `memberships` row. Their personal org, its exams and its Pro meter remain invisible to the school forever.
decisions.rationale: This is the single most common real case in our market: a teacher already uses us personally, then her school buys the institution tier. Creating a second account splits her history; merging silently hands a school her private data. Multi-org membership with an org switcher is the only answer that is honest to both parties, and it costs nothing because decision 5 already put org_id on every table.
decisions.alternativeRejected: GoTrue's built-in behaviour (422 email_exists), which simply cannot complete this flow; and 'convert the personal org into the school org', which would transfer a person's own data to their employer without consent — squarely against Saudi PDPL's explicit-consent-only posture (no legitimate-interest basis exists in the PDPL, and SDAIA has issued dozens of enforcement decisions since the grace period ended 14 Sep 2024).

decisions.decision: Email enumeration is removed by construction, not mitigated: no public endpoint accepts an email address. The only unauthenticated surface is `GET /invite/:selector` and `POST /invite/:selector/accept`. Every invalid state — expired, consumed, revoked, superseded, never existed — returns the identical body `{ "code": "invitation_invalid" }` with a constant-time path (always perform a dummy SHA-256 + timingSafeEqual against a fixed 32-byte value on the miss branch). Admin-side invite creation returns a uniform `pending` for every address and never discloses whether an account exists; the only distinguishable outcome is `already_member_of_this_org`, which the admin can already see in their own roster.
decisions.rationale: An oracle you never build cannot be tuned wrong later. Withholding existence even from the org admin costs us nothing (the admin does not need to know) and prevents the obvious abuse: buying one 25-seat licence to test 200 email addresses a day against our user base.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Generic messages on an endpoint that still takes an email (the usual advice). Response-time and side-effect differences leak anyway, and the endpoint invites future 'helpful' error messages.

decisions.decision: Password policy: minimum 15 characters, no composition rules, Unicode NFKC normalisation applied identically at set and at sign-in, HIBP Pwned Passwords range API (5-char SHA-1 prefix, `Add-Padding: true`) called from our Edge Function and failing open with a logged event, plus a local blocklist (the school's display name and email domain, the user's email local part, the top ~200 Arabic/Saudi-context strings). Supabase `PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` set to 15 (its default is 6, per supabase/auth README) and `PASSWORD_REQUIRED_CHARACTERS` left empty. No forced rotation, no security questions, no SMS.
decisions.rationale: ASVS 5.0 §6.2.1 (verified verbatim from OWASP/ASVS 5.0/en/0x15-V6-Authentication.md: 8 minimum, 15 strongly recommended), §6.2.5 (no composition rules), §6.2.12 (breached-password check), and NIST SP 800-63 Rev.4, finalised mid-2025 and governing through 2026, which PLAN §7 already cites. We run the HIBP check ourselves because Supabase's built-in leaked-password protection is a paid-plan feature (TECH-STACK note 7), and a security control must not be a billing line item. NFKC matters more in Arabic than in English: presentation forms, tatweel and combining marks give the same visual password several byte sequences, and Supabase verifies the hash, so our wrapper must normalise on both paths or users lock themselves out.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Dropping to ASVS's literal 8-character floor for invited members (weaker than our own consumer accounts, for accounts that hold *more* people's data), and pre-hashing passwords client-side (SHA-256 → base64, 44 ASCII chars) to escape the 72-byte cap: one code path that forgets to pre-hash, or any use of a Supabase-hosted recovery page, permanently locks the user out.

decisions.decision: Record an explicit, documented non-conformance with ASVS 5.0 §6.2.9 ('passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted') for Arabic-script passwords, and enforce the limit as a byte check with an Arabic error message that states the character count actually available.
decisions.rationale: Verified in supabase/auth `internal/api/password.go`: `// BCrypt hashed passwords have a 72 character limit` / `const MaxPasswordLength = 72`, and it rejects rather than silently truncates. Arabic letters are 2 bytes in UTF-8, so an Arabic passphrase is capped at 36 characters and a Latin one at 72. In an Arabic-first product this is a real, user-visible ceiling, and a validator that counts characters instead of bytes would show 'valid' and then get a 422 from Auth. This is the kind of thing that must be written down rather than discovered by a teacher at 7am.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Silently trimming to 72 bytes (produces a password that works on set and fails on the next device, and can cut an Arabic character in half), or claiming ASVS conformance we do not have.

decisions.decision: Authorization for institution data reads from the `memberships` table live, via a `STABLE SECURITY DEFINER` function, not from an `org_id` JWT claim. Policies become `org_id in (select app.member_org_ids())`, deny-by-default retained. The custom access token hook still stamps `org_id`, `role` and the membership list, but those claims are UI hints only. **This is an explicit departure from the PLAN §7 snippet** `using (org_id = (select auth.jwt()->>'org_id')::uuid)`.
decisions.rationale: With a JWT claim, revoking a teacher who has just been dismissed leaves her reading the school's results until her access token expires — 3600s by default, and Supabase discourages going below 300s. With a live membership lookup, revocation is effective on the next statement. The cost is one indexed lookup per policy evaluation, made once per statement by wrapping the call in `(select ...)` so Postgres treats it as an InitPlan. The claim also cannot express multi-org membership, which decision 5 above makes mandatory the moment a teacher belongs to both her personal org and her school.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Keeping the claim as the authorization source and shortening JWT expiry to 300s — it multiplies refresh traffic on an offline-first app that syncs in bursts, and it still leaves a five-minute window on the one action (dismissal) where minutes matter.

decisions.decision: Seats: default 25 per institution licence, sold in blocks, hard cap 200 members per org in the first release. Above 200 we do not scale email invitations — we require SSO/SCIM (Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace for Education, both already the identity provider in Saudi schools).
decisions.rationale: A Saudi government school runs roughly 30–45 teachers, so 25 covers a department or a small school and 200 covers the largest secondary schools plus their supervisors. From my angle the cap is a blast-radius control: a compromised admin account can emit at most 200 invitation emails from our sending domain, and our domain reputation is the asset that makes every invitation in the product deliverable. Past 200 the buyer is a district education office, where hand-typed email invitations are the wrong mechanism anyway — joiners and leavers must come from their directory, or revocation will silently lag reality.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Unlimited seats with a per-invite rate limit. It sells a promise (a whole district on email invites) whose failure mode is a stale roster nobody notices — ex-employees keeping access is the classic institutional finding, and rate limits do not address it.

schemaChanges.change: id uuid pk (UUIDv7 generated in app — Supabase is PG17, no native uuidv7()), org_id uuid not null references orgs on delete cascade, email citext not null, invitee_name text not null, role text not null default 'member' check (role in ('admin','member')), quota_papers int null, selector bytea not null, verifier_hash bytea not null, activation_pin_hash bytea null, pin_attempts smallint not null default 0, status text not null default 'pending' check (status in ('pending','accepted','revoked','superseded','expired','reported')), expires_at timestamptz not null, invited_by uuid not null references users(id), created_at timestamptz not null default now(), sent_count smallint not null default 1, last_sent_at timestamptz not null default now(), accepted_at timestamptz, accepted_user_id uuid references users(id), accepted_ip_hash bytea, superseded_by uuid references org_invitations(id)
schemaChanges.why: The invitation must be a first-class, auditable object: it carries the quota the admin allocated before the person exists, the role they will get, who invited them, and its own lifecycle. `verifier_hash` never holds a reversible secret; `accepted_ip_hash` is an HMAC under a daily-rotating key so the acceptance notice can say 'from a new location' without putting an IP in the database (PLAN §7: no PII in logs).

schemaChanges.change: create unique index invitations_selector_uq on org_invitations(selector); create unique index invitations_one_pending on org_invitations(org_id, email) where status = 'pending'; create index invitations_email_recent on org_invitations(email, created_at desc); create index invitations_expiry_sweep on org_invitations(expires_at) where status = 'pending'
schemaChanges.why: Selector lookup must be O(1) and collision-proof. One pending invitation per (org, email) makes 'resend' unambiguous and makes double-invite a no-op rather than two live tokens. The email+created_at index powers the anti-spam counters (3 per (org,email) per 24h, 10 per email across all orgs per 24h). The partial expiry index makes the hourly sweep that flips pending→expired cheap at any table size.

schemaChanges.change: org_id uuid, user_id uuid, role text not null check (role in ('owner','admin','member')), status text not null default 'active' check (status in ('active','revoked')), seat_quota_papers int null, invited_from uuid references org_invitations(id), joined_at timestamptz not null, revoked_at timestamptz, revoked_by uuid, primary key (org_id, user_id); create index memberships_by_user on memberships(user_id) where status='active'
schemaChanges.why: This is the object every RLS policy consults, so it must be small and indexed by user_id. Keeping revoked rows rather than deleting preserves the audit chain and makes re-invitation of a former teacher a state change with history rather than a fresh anonymous row.

schemaChanges.change: add kind text not null default 'personal' check (kind in ('personal','institution')), display_name text, seats int not null default 1, require_activation_pin boolean not null default false, admins_see_member_results boolean not null default true, email_domain text null, invites_frozen_at timestamptz null
schemaChanges.why: PLAN §5 has `orgs(id, owner_id)` only. `kind` is what makes 'one teacher = one org' and 'a school' the same row shape. `email_domain`, when set, means an invitation outside it needs a second explicit confirmation from the admin — the cheapest defence against inviting an address you do not control. `invites_frozen_at` is the kill switch when abuse reports cross threshold.

schemaChanges.change: Change primary key from (org_id, month) to (org_id, user_id, device_id, month); columns org_id, user_id, device_id text, month date, papers_graded int not null default 0, synced_at timestamptz. Org and per-member totals become SUM() over this table.
schemaChanges.why: DEPARTURE from PLAN §5, and an extension of decisions 4 and 5 rather than a contradiction. Quota allocation between invited members is impossible without per-member counting, and PLAN's own rule that the counter syncs cumulatively and is never overwritten only holds per device — with one teacher on a phone and a laptop, two devices writing (org_id, month) would erase each other's count. Per-device rows sum losslessly and keep the merge rule trivial: max() per device row, sum across rows.

schemaChanges.change: id uuid pk (v7), org_id uuid not null, actor_user_id uuid, action text not null, target_type text, target_id uuid, meta jsonb, created_at timestamptz not null default now(); plus a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises an exception, and REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_log FROM authenticated, anon. Actions: invitation.created / .resent / .revoked / .accepted / .expired / .reported, membership.role_changed / .revoked, quota.allocated, member_results.viewed.
schemaChanges.why: PLAN §7 already requires an append-only audit trail for grade edits; institutions extend it to the acts that carry power over another person. `member_results.viewed` is the one that matters in a school: an administrator reading a teacher's class results is a legitimate act that must leave a trace, which is also how we answer a PDPL data-subject question without guesswork.

schemaChanges.change: add default_org_id uuid null references orgs(id)
schemaChanges.why: A teacher can now be in her personal org and her school. The switcher needs a landing default, and the mobile app needs to know which encrypted database to open at launch.

schemaChanges.table: scans, exams, templates, students, answer_keys, usage (RLS policies)
schemaChanges.change: Replace `using (org_id = (select auth.jwt()->>'org_id')::uuid)` with `using (org_id in (select app.member_org_ids()))`, where `create function app.member_org_ids() returns setof uuid language sql stable security definer set search_path = '' as $$ select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = (select auth.uid()) and status = 'active' $$;`
schemaChanges.why: DEPARTURE from the PLAN §7 snippet, stated in decision 9: revocation must take effect on the next statement, not at the next token refresh, and a scalar claim cannot represent membership in two orgs. PLAN §11 acceptance criterion 4 (an automated test proving cross-org reads fail) is unchanged and gains a second case: a revoked member's read must fail with an unexpired access token in hand.

schemaChanges.change: Add a second predicate for role 'member': `and (owner_user_id = (select auth.uid()) or (select app.org_admin_can_view(org_id)))`, plus a new `owner_user_id uuid not null` column on exams and scans.
schemaChanges.why: Least privilege inside the org, which is the actual best practice in institutional grading systems: a teacher sees her own exams, an admin sees the org's only when `orgs.admins_see_member_results` is true, and the member is shown that setting in plain Arabic on the invitation acceptance screen. Without `owner_user_id`, 'my exams' and 'the school's exams' are indistinguishable and every member sees every class's results by default.

schemaChanges.change: Enforce in the Edge Function against the indexes above: per org 60 invitations/hour and 200/day; per (org, email) 3 sends/24h; per email address 10 sends/24h globally; per selector 10 failed POST accepts/hour then the invitation is killed and must be reissued; activation PIN 5 attempts then dead.
schemaChanges.why: Supabase's own mail path is not a defence: the built-in SMTP service is capped at 2 messages/hour and is explicitly not for production, and custom SMTP starts at 30/hour (raiseable) — a 200-seat onboarding needs a real provider, so the abuse ceiling has to be ours. `SMTP_MAX_FREQUENCY` defaults to 900s per user in supabase/auth, which does nothing about one admin blasting 200 different addresses.

schemaChanges.change: PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 15; PASSWORD_REQUIRED_CHARACTERS = ''; Email OTP expiration = 3600s (recovery and magic links only — invitations no longer use it); disable public sign-up for institution email domains? no — keep public sign-up on, but institution membership is unreachable except through invitation redemption; custom SMTP on a dedicated transactional subdomain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC p=reject; click-tracking and open-tracking OFF on the invitation template.
schemaChanges.why: The Supabase default minimum is 6 (verified in the supabase/auth README), so leaving it alone quietly nullifies our policy on any code path that calls Auth directly. Tracking must be off because ESP link rewriting replaces the URL and commonly drops the `#fragment` — which is where our verifier lives; this must be verified once against a seeded Outlook/Gmail mailbox before launch, not assumed.

schemaChanges.change: One SQLCipher database file per (user, org): `tc_<org_id>.db`, its 256-bit key in expo-secure-store under `tc.dbkey.<org_id>`. On a membership revoke observed during any authenticated sync, the app closes, deletes and re-creates nothing for that org and drops the key.
schemaChanges.why: PLAN §7 gives one encrypted local DB per device; with multi-org membership that would put a school's results in the same file as a teacher's private org. Separate files also make revocation a file deletion. The honest limit, in the same spirit as decision 4: a revoked teacher who stays offline keeps the local copy until the device next reaches the network. We accept and write that down rather than pretending server-side revocation reaches an offline device.

risks.risk: The invitation link is exactly as strong as the invitee's mailbox. A forwarded mail, a shared staffroom inbox (very common in schools), or an ESP compromise lets the holder set the password and become that member.
risks.mitigation: Optional per-org `require_activation_pin`: the admin sees a 6-digit PIN in the dashboard and hands it over out of band (in person or WhatsApp); it is mandatory, regardless of the org setting, for any invitation carrying role='admin'. 5 attempts then the invitation dies. That is ASVS 5.0 §6.5.4's 20-bit out-of-band code with real rate limiting, layered on top of the 256-bit link rather than replacing it. Plus: an acceptance notice to both the admin and the invited address, instant revoke that bites on the next statement (decision 9), and role='member' with no org-wide read as the default.

risks.risk: An administrator invites an address they do not control — a typo that reaches a stranger, a teacher's personal Gmail who never agreed, or a deliberate nuisance. Under Saudi PDPL there is no legitimate-interest basis; explicit consent is the only one, and SDAIA has been issuing enforcement decisions since the grace period closed in September 2024.
risks.mitigation: The landing page names the school, the inviting person and the date, and carries a prominent 'I do not know this school' button that revokes the invitation immediately, blocks that (org, email) pair for 90 days and increments an org abuse counter; 5 reports in 30 days sets `orgs.invites_frozen_at` pending human review. If `orgs.email_domain` is set, an invitation outside it requires a second explicit confirmation from the admin. The admin's attestation checkbox is weak on its own but records intent in the audit log, which is what turns a complaint into a resolvable incident.

risks.risk: Invitation spam burns our sending domain's reputation, and once transactional mail from our domain lands in Saudi school spam folders, every invitation in the product silently fails.
risks.mitigation: Layered caps enforced by us, not by the mail provider (60/hour and 200/day per org, 3 per (org,email) per 24h, 10 per address per 24h globally); a dedicated transactional subdomain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC p=reject, kept separate from any marketing sending so one cannot poison the other; bounce and complaint webhooks that auto-freeze an org's invitations at a 5% hard-bounce rate; and a pre-launch deliverability test into real Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace for Education tenants, since those two are the market.

risks.risk: Link scanners and prefetchers consume or corrupt the flow. Beyond burning tokens (mitigated by POST-only consumption), an ESP that rewrites URLs for click tracking can strip the `#fragment`, which would silently destroy every invitation because the verifier lives there.
risks.mitigation: Click and open tracking disabled on the invitation template, and a launch-blocking test that sends a real invitation into seeded Outlook, Gmail and a Defender-for-Office tenant and asserts the fragment survives. Fallback if any provider still mangles it: fall back to `?v=` for that template only and accept the log-hygiene cost, with the verifier redacted at the edge — but only after the failure is proven, never pre-emptively.

risks.risk: Revoked access lingers. A dismissed teacher keeps reading school data because a JWT claim has not refreshed, or because her phone holds an encrypted local copy and never comes online.
risks.mitigation: Server side is solved by construction: RLS reads `memberships` live, so the next statement fails even with an unexpired token, and PLAN §11 criterion 4 gains a second automated case proving it. Device side cannot be solved without breaking offline-first, so it is documented as accepted, exactly as decision 4 documents the meter: local DB is per-org, deleted with its key on the first authenticated sync after revocation, and the admin UI states plainly that a device that never reconnects keeps its last copy.

risks.risk: Institution accounts concentrate value: one compromised org admin can invite, promote, reallocate every teacher's quota and (where enabled) read the whole school's results, and none of that is visible to anyone else.
risks.mitigation: Every privileged act writes to the append-only audit_log, including `member_results.viewed`; the org owner receives a digest of admin actions; role changes to 'admin' require the activation PIN path; and members see, on the acceptance screen and in settings, a plain-Arabic statement of exactly what administrators of this school can see about them. Transparency to the affected teacher is the control that scales when the admin is the attacker.

result.rejected: The tempting wrong answer is the four-line version: call `supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email, { data: { org_id, role } })`, let GoTrue mail the link, read `org_id` out of the user's metadata into the JWT, and keep PLAN §7's policy `using (org_id = auth.jwt()->>'org_id')`. It looks like it uses the platform properly and it is what almost every Supabase tutorial shows. It is wrong four times over, and I verified each against the source rather than recalling it. (1) The `data` payload lands in `user_metadata`, which the end user can rewrite themselves — `internal/api/user.go` applies `params.Data` for any authenticated caller and gates only `app_metadata` behind `isAdmin` — so a teacher can set her own org_id and read another school's results. That single line is the worst failure the tier could have. (2) The stored invite token is `sha256.Sum224(email + otp)` (`internal/crypto/crypto.go`) and `/verify` accepts exactly that stored string as `token_hash` (`internal/api/verify.go`): the database column is a live bearer credential, replayable from any backup, seeded by a ~20-bit OTP. (3) `internal/api/invite.go` returns `ErrorCodeEmailExists` for a confirmed user, which both leaks account existence and hard-fails our most common case — the teacher who already has a personal account — leaving the admin with no path forward and us with no membership object to attach. (4) The link's lifetime is the project-wide Email OTP expiration, shared with password recovery, so any expiry that suits a week of school invitations also lengthens every recovery link on the product. The second, quieter temptation is to gate PDF-file grading (finding 36) as the 'institution scanning feature' because it sits next to the scanner in the roadmap. That would be a genuine breach of decision 1 rather than a scoping of it: the file format is what the free teacher on a school copier already has. Gate the driver-attached hardware path and the desktop helper that carries it; never gate the file.

result.area: Pricing and seat model for the Institutions tier (باقة المؤسسات)
result.recommendation: Add a third tier called **مؤسسات / Institutions** (not "Business", never "Enterprise"), sold as **banded seats, prepaid, one 12-month term, invoiced in SAR ex-VAT**, with **25 seats as the base band at SAR 2,250/year (SAR 90/seat, ≈USD 600)**. Two bands above it: **مدرسة / School, 100 seats, SAR 7,000** (SAR 70/seat) and **مجمّع / Campus, 300 seats, SAR 16,500** (SAR 55/seat); above 300 an **اتفاقية / Agreement** quote with a hard floor of SAR 50/seat. Add-on seats mid-term are sold at the band's per-seat rate prorated by whole months. Funnel is a **5-seat, one-semester, fully-featured free pilot, one per email domain, ever**. 25 is the base because 513,000 teachers ÷ 31,412 schools = **16.3 teachers per average Saudi school**, so the modal buyer never needs a second PO line; because it clears ZipGrade's verified 10-code institutional minimum so the deal cannot be reframed as "25 codes for $175"; and because it is exactly one Saudi university department (15–40 faculty plus TAs). Against the 6.99 USD/teacher/year anchor we are 3.4× per seat at 25, 2.7× at 100, 2.1× at 300 — a deliberately **converging** multiple, which is what a procurement officer expects to see as volume rises. That premium is defensible because we are not selling the same thing: ZipGrade's institutional route is bulk license codes emailed to an "admin", with purchase orders accepted **from US school districts only** (verified) — it literally cannot transact with a Saudi school. We sell the console, the invite flow, quota allocation, the scanner batch pipeline, a ZATCA-compliant invoice carrying their 15-digit TRN and their PO reference, and a 30-day grace period. Meanwhile every genuinely institutional comparable in 2026 prices *higher* per seat than us: Gradient (ex-GradeCam) at $3.00/student/year with a one-time setup fee works out to ~$45/teacher in a 600-student, 40-teacher school; Gradescope institutional starts ~$3/student; Akindi is $3.50/student with packages from $2,800/year; ESGI is $288–$364 per teacher per year. At $24/seat we sit far below the institutional band and far above the consumer anchor, which is the only place this tier can live. **Non-recurring billing survives contact with the institutional buyer and is in fact an advantage** — a school or government budget is annual and cannot commit to an auto-renewing card charge, and procurement departments actively distrust auto-renew — but it needs two changes it does not need for a consumer: a proforma quote (عرض سعر, 30-day validity) issued automatically at **T-90 days** with reminders at T-45 and T-14 against the **31 August** term boundary, and a **30-day post-expiry grace** in which the org drops to the free meter (100 papers/month org-wide) rather than dying, so nobody loses an exam week while a PO sits in finance. **All verification was via WebSearch on 2026-08-14; direct WebFetch to zipgrade.com, gradientk12.com, mastery-grade.com, salla.sa, shop.right.sa and mosahih.com was blocked by this session's egress policy, so vendor prices come from search-result snippets of those vendors' own pricing and support pages, not from the live pages, and should be re-confirmed by a human before they are printed on a rate card.

decisions.decision: The no-gates rule (PLAN.md §12-1) is SCOPED TO THE CONSUMER PRODUCT and stays fully intact there. Institutions is a different product for a different buyer. The rule is not broken, but I am departing from PLAN.md §12's opening sentence «باقتان لا أكثر» (two plans, no more) and I say so explicitly.
decisions.rationale: The recorded reason for the rule is precise and it is about a person: a feature-comparison table invites A TEACHER to weigh us against a mature $6.99 app. That reasoning describes a teacher paying out of pocket and comparing two listings in an app store. A school buying 100 seats with a purchase order never asks «what am I missing versus ZipGrade» — ZipGrade cannot accept their purchase order at all (POs from US school districts only, verified). They ask «can 100 teachers be provisioned, controlled and invoiced». The rule's reason does not reach that buyer, so the rule does not either. And the plan already anticipated this: PLAN.md §0 lists «حساب مدير» and «اشتراكات مدارس» as خارج النطاق (لاحقاً) — deferred, not rejected — and mandates org_id in every table from day one for exactly this purpose. §12's «two plans» and §0's deferred school subscriptions were already in tension in the existing document; I am resolving it, not breaking it. The binding replacement rule: WE GATE ADDITIONS INTO THE INSTITUTION TIER, WE NEVER WITHDRAW ANYTHING FROM THE CONSUMER TIERS. Free and Pro on the day Institutions ships have exactly what they had the day before.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: keeping literally two plans and selling institutions a bag of 25 Pro licences, ZipGrade-style. That is the competitor's actual institutional product and it is the friction we are selling against — 25 codes to chase, no console, no quota, no invoice. Also rejected: unlocking the scanner on Pro to preserve the no-gates rule intact, which destroys the only capability that makes the tier worth 3.4× the anchor.

decisions.decision: The gate is at the DEVICE DRIVER, not at the image. PDF import (COMPETITIVE-NOTES finding 36, «صحح ملف PDF») ships FREE and ungated in both consumer tiers. The Institutions tier gates only: direct TWAIN/eSCL/ICA device driving, batches over 25 pages, and multi-teacher batch reconciliation.
decisions.rationale: This is what makes the feature gate stable instead of a running argument. A teacher with a home ScanSnap iX1600 scans a class to PDF, drops the file in, and gets grades — no lock icon, no upgrade badge, PLAN.md §12-1 rule 1 («الواجهة تبقى خالية من الأقفال») literally preserved. What she cannot do is drive the scanner from inside the app and push a 100-page ADF batch (fi-8170: 70ppm, 100-page ADF) through multi-teacher reconciliation. core-omr already takes an image and does not care where it came from, so this costs us nothing in the engine; the institutional cost is entirely in the driver layer, the batch queue and the reconciliation UI — which is exactly where the price sits.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: gating «scanned images» wholesale. It would mean a Pro teacher who scans to PDF gets a paywall on a file she already has, which is a withdrawal of a capability finding 36 already promised, and the first credible accusation that we broke our own rule.

decisions.decision: Base band = 25 seats at SAR 2,250/year ex-VAT. No band smaller than 25. Ever.
decisions.rationale: 25 covers the average Saudi school (16.3 teachers) plus the admin plus growth, so the modal buyer signs one PO line and never comes back for a second. It is one Saudi university department. It clears ZipGrade's 10-code floor so we are never compared code-for-code. And SAR 2,250 is roughly SAR 187/month — below a school's monthly photocopier toner, comfortably inside a private principal's discretionary operating budget, and three orders of magnitude below the SAR 1,000,000 direct-purchase threshold that the new Government Tenders and Procurement Law set when the Council of Ministers approved it on 5 August 2026 (raised from SAR 100,000), so a government buyer never needs a competitive tender for us. Refusing to sell below 25 is itself a signal: a vendor with no 5-seat or 10-seat band is a vendor that sells to institutions, not to teacher groups, and that signal is worth more than the marginal small deal.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: a 10-seat entry band at ~SAR 900. It puts us directly beside ZipGrade's 10 × $6.99 = $69.90 and we lose that comparison badly on price while winning it on nothing the buyer can see in a table. Also rejected: a first-year 20% discount to seed the funnel — Saudi buyers will expect it at every renewal and it is very hard to unwind. The 5-seat free pilot does the seeding without poisoning the rate card.

decisions.decision: Term is 12 months, prepaid, and institutions may align it to the academic year ending 31 August. Mid-year purchases prorate by WHOLE MONTHS to the following 31 August at band price ÷ 12.
decisions.rationale: Saudi public schools returned to a TWO-semester year from 1447/1448 (2025-26) by Cabinet decision, and 2026-27 is two semesters, 180 school days / 38 weeks. A 31 August boundary puts every institutional renewal into the June–August window, which is precisely when school budgets are set and POs are raised. Clustering renewals there is a feature, not a load problem. Whole-month proration, not daily, because a PO line item with three decimal places gets bounced by finance.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: rolling 12-month terms from activation date. It scatters renewals across the calendar, so half of them land mid-semester when there is no budget line open and no one authorised to sign, which converts a renewal into a churn event for purely administrative reasons.

decisions.decision: Non-recurring billing is KEPT for institutions (PLAN.md §12-1 decision 2 holds), plus a T-90/T-45/T-14 proforma quote cadence and a 30-day post-expiry grace at the free meter (100 papers/month for the whole org).
decisions.rationale: A Saudi school or university budget is annual and cannot legally commit to an auto-renewing card charge; procurement departments treat auto-renew as a liability, not a convenience. So the consumer decision transfers unchanged and is actually a selling point here. What does NOT transfer is «prompt at the end of the term» — a school prompted on the last day loses its seats while the PO grinds through finance for six weeks. The 90-day proforma (عرض سعر, valid 30 days, quoting the PO reference back) lands before the budget closes; the grace period means the worst case is a slow month, not a dead exam week. The grace costs us almost nothing because our marginal cost is near zero.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: auto-renewing annual subscriptions with a card on file, the SaaS default. No Saudi government entity and few private schools will put a card on file for a recurring charge; it converts a purchasable line item into a policy exception. Also rejected: hard cut-off at expiry, which punishes the buyer for our own billing calendar.

decisions.decision: The org's grading is UNLIMITED. The meter is not a revenue lever at institutional scale; the SEAT is. Enforcement: a seat binds to one verified person, max 3 concurrent devices, max 2 reassignments per term, plus an admin-facing outlier report.
decisions.rationale: Metering papers at institutional scale would earn us nothing (all processing is on-device, marginal cost ~0) while re-importing the offline-overrun problem of PLAN.md §12-2 multiplied by 300 seats. The real risk to the band ladder is 25 seats shared across 80 teachers, and that is a seat problem. 3 devices honours §12-1 decision 3 («مستخدم واحد بأجهزة متعددة»: phone + tablet + laptop) while catching a shared login. The outlier report is shown to the ADMIN, not enforced by us — the admin is the one person with both the incentive and the standing to fix a shared account, and policing it ourselves would mean a network check before scanning, which §12-2 forbids.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: an org-wide monthly paper cap sized to the band (e.g. 25 seats × 500 papers). It re-creates the offline-enforcement problem the plan explicitly closed, it punishes the exam-week spike that is the entire shape of this product's demand, and it earns nothing.

decisions.decision: The admin's quota allocation exists as the product owner asked, but its DEFAULT is «no limit» and its purpose is internal visibility, not our revenue: per-seat monthly caps, optional, plus a shared unallocated org pool.
decisions.rationale: The product owner asked for quota allocation between invited accounts and it is genuinely useful — a university department caps a TA seat, a school spots the seat grading 4,000 papers a month. But if it defaults to ON, every institution ships with 25 artificial walls inside a product whose founding rule is that the interface has no locks in it. Default off, admin opts in, and the per-seat usage numbers are visible to the admin from day one whether or not any cap is set.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: mandatory per-seat allocation where the band's seat count divides an org paper budget. It makes the admin do arithmetic on our behalf for a resource that costs us nothing, and the first teacher to hit a wall mid-exam-week blames us, not her admin.

decisions.decision: Price in SAR as primary (USD secondary at the 3.75 peg), ex-VAT, with 15% VAT as a separate line and both parties' tax numbers on the document. Sell institution seats WEB-ONLY, never through in-app purchase.
decisions.rationale: A foreign-currency line item invites an FX question in Saudi procurement that nobody wants to answer; the riyal peg makes the dual display free. VAT is 15% and a Saudi tax invoice must carry the 15-digit TRN. Selling on the web keeps institution revenue entirely outside the App Store / Play commission — B2B SaaS sold elsewhere has always been permitted to skip IAP, and Apple's 13 August 2026 filing proposing up to 15% on US link-outs is still unapproved and does not reach a web-only B2B sale. Rails: Moyasar or HyperPay for Mada/card (Stripe is NOT available to a Saudi-resident merchant — it is not SAMA-licensed for Mada acquiring), and SADAD plus bank transfer as the primary institutional rail, since SADAD is specifically the invoice-based B2B mechanism.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: USD-only pricing through a merchant-of-record like Paddle to dodge Saudi tax registration. It hands 5%+ to the MoR, produces an invoice a Saudi school's finance office may not accept, and leaves us unable to issue a ZATCA-cleared document when they ask for one.

decisions.decision: Cap self-serve Pro at 5 licences per transaction and per payment instrument; beyond that the flow routes to Institutions. Recommend Pro at SAR 39/year ex-VAT (≈$10.40).
decisions.rationale: The crossover is real and I want it stated rather than discovered: at SAR 39, twenty-five Pro licences cost SAR 975 against SAR 2,250 for the Department band, so anything under ~58 teachers is nominally cheaper bought individually. I am not closing that with price — an institution buying 25 Pro licences gets no console, no invoice, no PO, no scanner, no grace period, and has to chase 25 people to redeem 25 codes, which is precisely ZipGrade's product and precisely the friction we sell against. I close it with the mechanic instead: the bulk-buy path simply does not exist self-serve. SAR 39 sits slightly above the SAR 26 anchor as PLAN.md §12-1 already recommends.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: raising Pro to SAR 90 so 25 × Pro equals the Department band. It taxes the individual teacher — our actual beachhead and the buyer the whole no-gates strategy was built for — to protect an institutional band she will never buy.

decisions.decision: Go-to-market sequence: private and international schools, university departments and training centres FIRST. Do not chase public MOE schools or Etimad in year one.
decisions.rationale: Etimad requires a Saudi commercial registration from the supplier, and since 1 January 2024 foreign bidders face a Regional Headquarters condition, with the only alternatives being a MISA investor licence or a Saudi commercial agent. Meanwhile a private or international school buys directly on its own authority — and these are the schools with the teacher counts our bands are cut for (Al Yasmin: 87 teaching staff; Yara: 132; Riyadh international schools average 1,568 students). 7,337 private schools is a large enough beachhead to prove the tier without a corporate structuring project. Register a Saudi CR and take VOLUNTARY VAT registration (below the SAR 375,000 mandatory threshold) before the first institution sale anyway, because the first school that asks for a رقم ضريبي and does not get one ends the conversation.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rejected: launching at public MOE schools because they are 24,075 of the 31,412 and the obvious volume. Without a Saudi CR we cannot even register on Etimad, so the pipeline would be entirely unclosable, and the ZATCA Phase 2 Wave 24 clearance obligation (30 June 2026 for turnover above SAR 375,000) arrives before the revenue does.

schemaChanges.change: Add kind text check in ('personal','institution'); plan text check in ('free','pro','inst_dept','inst_school','inst_campus','inst_agreement'); seats_purchased int not null default 1; term_start date; term_end date; grace_until date; legal_name text; vat_number text (15-digit KSA TRN, nullable, check length 15 when not null); billing_country char(2) default 'SA'; currency char(3) default 'SAR'.
schemaChanges.why: PLAN.md §5 has orgs(id, owner_id) only. A PO-driven sale needs exactly three things that do not exist today: how many seats were bought, when the term ends, and the buyer's tax number. grace_until is a separate column from term_end because the 30-day grace is a distinct state the client must render differently (free meter, banner, no new invites), and deriving it from term_end + interval scatters the business rule across every query.

schemaChanges.change: NEW: memberships(org_id, user_id, role text check in ('owner','admin','teacher'), seat_state text check in ('invited','active','suspended','released'), invited_by uuid, invited_at, activated_at, deactivated_at, monthly_quota int null, reassignment_count smallint default 0, primary key (org_id, user_id)).
schemaChanges.why: PLAN.md §12-1 decision 3 says the licence is per PERSON. A seat must therefore be the membership row, not a column on users — one human can hold a seat in an institution and still own a personal free org without either bleeding into the other. Exactly three roles: a fourth invites a permissions matrix nobody asked for. monthly_quota nullable, null meaning unlimited, so the default costs no row and no wall.

schemaChanges.change: NEW: invitations(id uuid_v7 pk, org_id, email citext, display_name text, role text, token_hash bytea not null, expires_at timestamptz not null, accepted_at, revoked_at, created_by, unique partial index on (org_id, lower(email)) where accepted_at is null and revoked_at is null).
schemaChanges.why: This is the product owner's flow: admin enters email + name, invitee receives a link to set a password. Store ONLY sha256 of a 32-byte random token, never the token, so a database read cannot mint sessions — consistent with §7's posture. Token lifetime 7 days, single use, invalidated the instant a password is set; a resend mints a new token and revokes the old one. The partial unique index stops an admin double-inviting the same person and burning a seat twice.

schemaChanges.change: Change primary key from (org_id, month) to (org_id, user_id, month, device_id). Keep papers_graded int and synced_at.
schemaChanges.why: §12-2 requires usage to sync as a CUMULATIVE counter so two devices never overwrite each other's count. Widening the key to include user_id and device_id makes that guarantee structural rather than procedural: each device owns exactly one row and only ever increments its own, org and per-seat totals are a SUM, and the last-writer-wins hazard disappears entirely. It also answers the question today's table cannot — «who graded these» — which is what the admin needs before allocating any quota.

schemaChanges.change: Add graded_by uuid (the membership user_id) and source text check in ('camera','pdf','scanner') not null default 'camera'.
schemaChanges.why: graded_by is the join that makes per-seat usage and the shared-seat outlier report possible; device_id alone cannot answer it once a person legitimately uses three devices. source is what makes the scanner gate auditable and, more importantly, provable in support: when a Pro teacher says the scanner is blocked, we can show her rows are source='pdf' and were graded normally. It also prices the tier honestly — we can report to an institution how many papers actually came through the batch pipeline they paid for.

schemaChanges.change: NEW: billing_documents(id uuid_v7 pk, org_id, kind text check in ('quote','invoice','credit_note'), number text unique not null, issued_at, due_at, valid_until, currency char(3), subtotal_halalas bigint, vat_halalas bigint, total_halalas bigint, buyer_vat_number text, buyer_legal_name text, po_reference text, seats int, band text, zatca_uuid uuid, zatca_hash bytea, zatca_cleared_at timestamptz, status text).
schemaChanges.why: A Saudi school requires an invoice carrying its own PO reference and both parties' tax numbers, and ZATCA Phase 2 requires a UUID, a cryptographic stamp and strictly sequential numbering on the document itself, with B2B invoices cleared before they are sent. Money is halalas as bigint, never real and never float — §5 uses real for scores, which is right there and wrong here. valid_until carries the 30-day proforma validity for the T-90 quote.

schemaChanges.change: NEW: seat_devices(org_id, user_id, device_id, first_seen, last_seen, primary key (org_id, user_id, device_id)) with a server-enforced cap of 3 rows per (org_id, user_id); the least-recently-seen row is evicted with an explicit notice, never silently.
schemaChanges.why: The 3-device rule is the only enforcement standing between a 25-seat band and 80 teachers sharing 25 logins, and it needs a home. Eviction must be visible for the same reason PLAN.md §4 rule 9 forbids inventing a value for a missing ID: a device silently losing access is indistinguishable from a bug, and the teacher will report it as one.

schemaChanges.change: NEW: pilots(email_domain citext primary key, org_id, started_at, ends_at, converted_at) enforcing one 5-seat semester pilot per domain, ever.
schemaChanges.why: Keyed on the email DOMAIN, not the admin's identity, because otherwise the same school re-pilots every semester through a different vice-principal's address. It is the cheapest possible abuse control and it is the only place the pilot rule can be enforced, since the org row is created fresh each time.

schemaChanges.change: Replace `using (org_id = (select auth.jwt()->>'org_id')::uuid)` with `using (org_id in (select org_id from memberships where user_id = auth.uid() and seat_state = 'active'))`, or keep the JWT fast path but re-issue the token with an org_ids array claim on every membership change.
schemaChanges.why: THIS IS A CORRECTION TO A DECISION ALREADY MADE, caused directly by the seat model, and I am flagging it rather than letting it be discovered. The existing policy assumes exactly one org per JWT. The moment a teacher holds both a personal org and an institution seat — the normal case, since she starts on Free and her school later invites her — a single org_id claim silently shows her the wrong org's data or hides her own. §7 calls isolation «أهم بند» and says one leak ends the project, so this cannot wait for the institution tier to ship. The §11 acceptance test (item 4) must be extended: a user who is a member of org A and org B must fail to read org C, AND must not see B's rows while acting in A.

schemaChanges.change: Extend the existing append-only audit log (§7) to cover seat lifecycle: invite issued, invite accepted, seat reassigned, seat suspended, quota changed, band changed, device evicted. Retain for the full term plus 12 months.
schemaChanges.why: §7 already mandates an append-only audit log for grade edits. An institution admin who can silently reassign a seat away from a teacher mid-term now controls access to that teacher's graded work, which is a materially bigger power than editing one grade. The admin needs the log as much as we do — the first dispute about who removed whom is otherwise unanswerable.

risks.risk: We cannot legally invoice a Saudi institutional buyer without a Saudi entity. Etimad registration requires a Saudi commercial registration, with a Regional Headquarters condition on foreign bidders since 1 January 2024. A school that asks for a رقم ضريبي on the invoice and does not get one ends the conversation on the spot.
risks.mitigation: Obtain a Saudi CR and take VOLUNTARY VAT registration before the first institution sale, well below the SAR 375,000 mandatory threshold, and stand up ZATCA Phase 2 clearance through HyperPay or an equivalent certified provider. Until that exists, sell only to private and international schools willing to accept a foreign invoice, and capture a verified 15-digit TRN before invoicing so the reverse-charge treatment is actually valid. Do not open any public-MOE or Etimad pipeline in year one — it is unclosable and it consumes the sales calendar.

risks.risk: Seat sharing collapses the band ladder: one school buys 25 seats and runs 80 teachers on them, so nobody ever reaches the 100-seat band and the entire price ladder becomes decorative.
risks.mitigation: Three layers, none of which requires a network check before scanning: 3 concurrent devices per seat (generous for phone + tablet + laptop, fatal for a shared login), at most 2 seat reassignments per term with the outgoing person's local SQLCipher key access revoked on next sync, and an admin-facing outlier report showing papers per seat per month. Enforcement is aimed at the admin, who has both the incentive and the standing to fix it. Explicitly accept, as §12-2 already does for the consumer meter, that a determined offline institution can exceed this, and record that acceptance so it is not reopened.

risks.risk: Non-recurring billing plus a late purchase order equals churn that has nothing to do with the product. The PO sits in finance for six weeks and the school's 100 seats expire in the middle of the semester.
risks.mitigation: Automatic proforma quote at T-90 against the 31 August boundary, reminders at T-45 and T-14, quote valid 30 days and quoting their own PO reference back to them; then a 30-day post-expiry grace in which the org falls back to the free meter (100 papers/month org-wide) instead of dying. Measure renewal specifically as «renewed before grace ended» rather than «renewed», so an administrative near-miss is visible as a problem rather than hidden inside a healthy-looking number.

risks.risk: Pro bulk-buying leaks under the Department band. At SAR 39 for Pro, twenty-five individual licences cost SAR 975 against SAR 2,250, so every school under roughly 58 teachers is nominally cheaper buying Pro seats one at a time.
risks.mitigation: Close it with the mechanic, not the price: cap self-serve Pro at 5 licences per transaction and per payment instrument, with anything beyond routed to Institutions. Do not raise Pro to defend the band — that taxes the individual teacher who is the beachhead. State the crossover (≈58 teachers) openly in the internal rate card so sales is never surprised by it, and answer it the way it should be answered: 25 Pro licences means 25 codes to chase, no console, no quota, no invoice, no scanner, no grace period.

risks.risk: A sophisticated buyer, especially a university, benchmarks us against Gradescope or Gradient quotes that are priced per student and demands the same basis. Per-seat then looks arbitrary or expensive to them at large student counts.
risks.mitigation: Answer with the architecture, which is the honest answer: our student table stores an optional name and an external id and no PII by design (§7), so we do not hold and will not demand the accurate roster that per-student billing requires — the privacy promise and the billing basis are the same decision. Then convert on their terms for the comparison only: SAR 7,000 for a 100-seat school of 1,500 students is SAR 4.67 per student per year, roughly $1.25, against Gradient's $3.00 and Akindi's $3.50. We win that comparison decisively; we simply refuse to bill on it.

risks.risk: The scanner gate erodes under pressure. A Pro teacher with a home ScanSnap escalates publicly, and the first person to say «you promised zero feature gates» is right unless the boundary is written down in advance.
risks.mitigation: Publish the boundary as a rule, in Arabic, on the pricing page, before anyone asks: PDF import is free forever in every tier; what Institutions buys is direct device control and batch reconciliation. Enforce the companion rule internally — additions may launch institution-only, but nothing that has ever shipped to Free or Pro is ever withdrawn — and keep scans.source so any individual dispute is settled by data in one query rather than by argument.

result.rejected: **Per-student pricing.** It is the single most tempting wrong answer here, because it genuinely is the 2026 majority practice in exactly this category — Gradient (ex-GradeCam, now GoGuardian) at $3.00 per student per year plus a one-time setup fee with unlimited teachers per building, Gradescope institutional from about $3 per student, Akindi at $3.50 per student with packages starting at $2,800 per year. The product owner asked me to «follow best practice in institutional grading systems», and per-student pricing is, on the evidence, what that phrase points at. It is still wrong for us, for three specific reasons. **First, it prices the one thing our architecture deliberately refuses to know.** PLAN.md §5 defines students(id, org_id, ext_id, name) with the name optional, and §7 calls data minimisation «أقوى حماية موجودة» — no national ID, no date of birth, no student photos, no uploaded images. Billing per student would require us to demand and audit an accurate roster, which means arguing with a school about whether its student count is honest, which means holding the very data we built the product's strongest security claim around not holding. The privacy promise and the billing basis are the same decision, and you cannot keep one while selling the other. **Second, it taxes the exact behaviour we just paid to encourage.** §0 moved CSV class-list import INTO the MVP because writing thirty names by hand is a harder entry barrier than building a sheet. Under per-student billing, every name a teacher imports raises her school's invoice — we would be charging for onboarding, and the rational response is to import fewer students, which breaks the roster the product depends on. **Third, the arithmetic lands in the wrong place for this market.** Riyadh international schools average 1,568 students; at $3 that is $4,704, about SAR 17,600 a year. A Saudi school with a standalone OMR corrector available for SAR 3,000 as a one-time capital purchase (DataLink 3000 at SAR 12,000 for the high end) will put those two numbers side by side, and a recurring line item four to six times the price of a machine it can buy once and keep is a conversation we lose before the demo. Per-seat at SAR 55–90 keeps us inside operating expenditure, where nobody compares us to hardware. Worth noting: per-student is not rejected as a *benchmark* — converted for comparison only, SAR 7,000 for a 100-seat, 1,500-student school is about SAR 4.67 (≈$1.25) per student per year, which beats every product above by better than half. We win that comparison and still decline to bill on it.

result.area: Bulk scanner ingestion for the Institutions tier: what school scanners actually emit, how a stack of hundreds of pages becomes hundreds of graded papers, and where that computation lives given the no-image-upload promise
result.recommendation: Build a file pipeline, not a scanner integration. In a Saudi school in 2026 the "advanced fast scanner" is one of three things and none of them talks to an app: a departmental copier (Canon imageRUNNER ADVANCE DX C3835i, 200 sheet single pass DADF, 270 ipm duplex, scan to SMB 3.0 / email / WebDAV), a sheetfed desktop unit on the exam committee PC (Ricoh fi-8170, 70 ppm / 140 ipm duplex at 200-300 dpi, 100 sheet ADF, rated 10,000 sheets a day; or ScanSnap iX2500, 45 ppm / 90 ipm, 100 sheet ADF, which replaced the discontinued iX1600 at 40/80), or a driverless eSCL network device (XML over HTTP, mDNS discovery, the Mopria specification behind AirScan and Mopria Scan). All three end the same way: a multi page file appears in a folder, a mailbox or a USB stick. So our ingestion contract is "a set of files at a location", and everything else is workflow. The bulk path runs entirely locally: in the web console, pdf.js (Apache 2.0, pdfjs-dist 6.2.x current as of late July 2026) rasterises pages into a pool of Web Workers where core-omr grades them, and on device it uses the OS pdfium wrappers (iOS PDFKit, Android PdfRenderer with PdfRendererPreV back-porting the Android V render API to API 30-34). Zero bytes leave the machine, and with connect-src 'self' that claim is auditable by the user in devtools, which is stronger evidence than "trust our server". Nothing is server side, and the phone is deliberately not the primary home for batches, because the file is on a Windows PC next to the copier and every convenient way to move 400 MB to a phone is a cloud, which would push users to upload the exact images we promised never to upload. core-omr gains exactly one new public function, gradePage(GraySource, {assumedDpi}), which the camera also calls three times under its existing agreement rule, so there is one pipeline and no duplicate engine. On the feature gate question: the gate is not "fast scanners", it is unattended multi operator batch operations. Grading a PDF up to 40 pages ships in the consumer product free and Pro alike, so no teacher ever sees a lock; institutions get folder watch, eSCL, hundreds of pages with resume, roster completeness reconciliation across classes, per operator audit and quota allocation. That scopes decision 1 to the consumer buyer, which PLAN section 12-1 already anticipated in writing, rather than breaking it.

decisions.decision: Treat ingestion as a file contract, not a device integration. We ship no TWAIN, SANE or ICA driver layer. v1 is drag and drop of files into the web console plus the OS file picker on device; v1.5 is a small signed desktop helper that watches the SMB drop folder; v2 adds an eSCL Scan button (which needs the same helper, because a browser cannot do mDNS discovery).
decisions.rationale: Verified by vendor spec pages: the copier route is scan to SMB 3.0 / FTP / WebDAV / email (Canon iR-ADV DX C3835i product info), the sheetfed route is a vendor driver such as PaperStream Capture or ScanSnap Home writing a file to a folder (pfu-us.ricoh.com fi-8170 and iX2500 pages), and only eSCL is a protocol we could drive ourselves (mopria.org eSCL specification, mDNS/DNS-SD discovery, XML over HTTP, per Mopria and the Debian eSCL wiki). Two of the three routes can never be driven by our software, so the file is the only universal surface. Scan to email is also self limiting: a 600 page 300 dpi colour batch is 300-500 MB against typical 5-10 MB MFP attachment caps, so it arrives split across several messages, which is why a batch must be defined as a set of files rather than one file.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Writing a native scanner driver layer (TWAIN on Windows, ICA on macOS, SANE on Linux). Rejected: it is a Windows binary plus a macOS binary before a single paper is graded, it does nothing for the copier route which is the dominant one in schools, and it delivers the same bytes we would get for free from a watched folder.

decisions.decision: The bulk path lives locally: in the browser page for the web console, and natively on the device app. Never on a server.
decisions.rationale: PLAN section 7 (data minimisation) and section 9 (near zero marginal cost) both rest on images never moving, and COMPETITIVE-NOTES 57 ties that directly to surviving a 26 SAR a year market anchor. Beyond strategy there is law: the Saudi PDPL has been in force since 14 September 2023 with a 14 September 2024 compliance deadline, has a separate Regulations on Personal Data Transfers outside the Kingdom, and SDAIA enforcement committees issued 48 violation decisions across 2025-2026 with power to suspend processing (iclg.com Saudi Arabia data protection chapter 2026, dlapiperdataprotection.com). Uploading images of Saudi students' handwritten names would convert a zero liability product into a cross border transfer question the moment our Supabase region sits outside KSA, and would require a DPA with every school.
decisions.alternativeRejected: A server side batch endpoint. It is by far the least code and it makes the file transport problem vanish, which is exactly why it is the tempting wrong answer. See the rejected field.

decisions.decision: core-omr gets exactly one new public entry point, not a second pipeline: gradePage(src: GraySource, opts: {assumedDpi?: number}): PageOutcome. The camera path calls the same function three times and applies its existing three-frames-agree rule on top of it.
decisions.rationale: The camera pipeline in PLAN section 4 is downscale, grayscale, adaptiveThreshold, contours, corner square filter, perspective warp to 1000x1414, decode the printed code, per bubble fill fraction. Only the first step and the frame lifecycle (frame.dispose in try/finally) are camera specific. A flatbed page arrives already flat with near perfect corners, so the warp is cheaper, not different. Keeping the agreement rule in the camera layer rather than in core-omr is the honest split: triple agreement compensates for video noise, and a 200 dpi scan has no second look.
decisions.alternativeRejected: A separate scan-file grading module that reimplements thresholding for 'document quality' input. Rejected because it would fork the accuracy surface: the golden set gates one engine at 99.7% and a second engine would ship ungated.

decisions.decision: v1 accepts multi page PDF and folders of JPEG/PNG. Multi page TIFF is detected, named, and refused with an instruction to change the copier's output format; real TIFF support waits for v2.
decisions.rationale: iOS ImageIO reads multi page TIFF natively, but Android's BitmapFactory does not decode TIFF at all (verified: decodeFile returns null for .tif), so the only options are a libtiff JNI wrapper such as Android-TiffBitmapFactory, which is a single maintainer project from the 2016 era, or a WASM decoder. One sentence of Arabic telling the exam officer to set the copier to PDF costs nothing and is reversible; an unmaintained native dependency in the grading path is not. Also reject mupdf.js for PDF: it is AGPL or commercial from Artifex, so a proprietary app needs a purchased licence, whereas pdf.js is Apache 2.0 and the OS renderers are free.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Shipping libtiff on Android in v1 for completeness. Rejected: TIFF is a legacy default that one settings change removes, and the dependency would sit inside the code path that our 99.7% accuracy gate protects.

decisions.decision: Reject pages whose implied resolution is below 150 dpi up front, recommend 200 dpi grayscale, and detect high compression / MRC PDF (JPXDecode, or a bitonal mask plus low resolution background) and warn before grading.
decisions.rationale: Our engine is millimetre based, so dpi is derived per page as pixels divided by MediaBox points over 72. At 150 dpi a 5 mm bubble is about 30 px across, which is workable; at 100 dpi it is 20 px and fill fraction gets noisy. Compact PDF and high compression PDF modes on Canon and Ricoh fleets segment the page into layers, and recomposition can shift edges by a pixel or two, which is precisely the measurement our threshold depends on. Failing loudly at import beats degrading silently at grading, which is the exact failure mode we criticised in the competitor (COMPETITIVE-NOTES 49).
decisions.alternativeRejected: Grading whatever arrives and letting the ambiguity flags absorb bad input. Rejected: it converts a fixable settings problem into a per paper review burden across hundreds of pages.

decisions.decision: Search rotation using the printed code, in the order 0, 180, 90, 270 degrees, and record rotation_applied per page.
decisions.rationale: Our four fiducials are identical 8x8 mm squares, so they are rotationally symmetric and cannot distinguish 0 from 180. The self describing printed code introduced in the 2026-08-14 devlog entry has a fixed orientation corner, so it is the disambiguator. Cost is at worst four decodes of a small region, not four full grades. This is a genuinely new requirement that the camera path never had, because a teacher holds a paper the right way up, and an ADF stack does not: without it the first real school batch will show several per cent unreadable pages.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Relying on the scanner's auto orientation. Rejected: vendor auto rotate is text and OCR driven and an answer sheet is mostly empty bubbles, so it either does nothing or guesses from the sparse Arabic header.

decisions.decision: Nothing is discarded. Every source page gets exactly one batch_pages row with one of six outcomes (graded, ambiguous, noSheet, geometryFailed, codeUnreadable, duplicate), and the product invariant, asserted in CI, is that a finished batch has count(batch_pages) equal to batches.page_count. Failures are reported by source page number.
decisions.rationale: Duplex feeding of single sided sheets means roughly half the images are blank backs, and vendor blank page removal is an ink coverage threshold that will also drop a lightly filled real answer sheet. Classifying rather than deleting is both safer and free, because a page with no decodable fiducial set and no printed code is definitionally not a paper. Page number is the addressing scheme because the recovery action is physical: pull sheet 47 out of the output tray. Grouping the blank backs as a single collapsed row keeps the report readable.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Enabling the scanner's blank page skip and reporting only successes. Rejected: it makes silent loss a configuration setting on someone else's hardware, and PLAN acceptance criterion 1 forbids silent errors.

decisions.decision: Keep a bounded derived preview for failed pages only: a 400x560 grayscale JPEG of about 25 KB plus the existing name crop, stored in the local SQLCipher database in batch_page_previews with a 7 day TTL, never placed in sync_queue. This is an explicit departure from the letter of PLAN section 7 and the public wording must change in the same release.
decisions.rationale: A 600 page batch produces failures that the teacher inspects minutes or hours later on a different screen, and a page number alone cannot tell 'page 112 was a blank back' from 'page 112 was a real paper scanned badly'. The alternative extremes both fail: keeping full page images means several hundred megabytes of student handwriting at rest with a retention policy we said we would never need, and keeping nothing makes the batch report unusable. Twenty failures at 25 KB is 500 KB, local, encrypted with the existing device bound key, expiring, and one tap purgeable. The published promise becomes: images are never uploaded, and in batch mode a low resolution thumbnail of pages that failed stays on your device until you close the batch. Departing quietly would make our own privacy page false, which is a worse outcome than amending it.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Keeping the promise verbatim by making previews opt in per batch, default off. Viable and worth offering as a setting, but rejected as the default because a batch review without thumbnails sends the operator back to a 600 sheet paper stack, which is the workflow the tier exists to remove.

decisions.decision: Resume and deduplicate a batch on idempotency key sha256(file bytes) plus page index, commit to SQLite one transaction per 50 papers, and stream pages one at a time with a worker concurrency of 4 on desktop and 2 on mobile.
decisions.rationale: This reuses the outbox idempotency design in PLAN section 6 rather than inventing a batch specific mechanism, and it makes re importing the same PDF after a crash resume instead of duplicating, which matters because the source file is still on disk since we never copied it. Memory: a 200 dpi grayscale A4 page is 1654x2339, about 3.9 MB, and 300 dpi is about 8.7 MB, so streaming at concurrency 4 peaks near 35 MB while rasterising the whole document would peak in the gigabytes. One worker owns the PDF document and posts transferable buffers to grader workers, because page decoding is cheap next to grading and duplicating the document object costs memory for nothing.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Rasterising the whole PDF to a temp directory first, then grading. Rejected on two counts: peak memory or disk, and it writes hundreds of unencrypted page images to disk, which is the privacy failure we are trying to avoid.

decisions.decision: The meter increments once per page whose outcome is graded or ambiguous, and never for noSheet, geometryFailed or codeUnreadable. Institution quota is allocated from an org pool to invited accounts and enforced with the same local first, last known balance rule as the consumer meter.
decisions.rationale: Duplex feeding roughly doubles page count against paper count, so a naive per page meter would silently halve an institution's purchased quota on the very devices this tier is sold for. Charging for pages we failed to read is also indefensible when the failure is usually our geometry check refusing bad input. Keeping the enforcement rule identical to PLAN section 12-2 means no second metering code path and no network dependency added to the scan loop.
decisions.alternativeRejected: Counting source pages, which is simpler to explain and matches what the scanner reports. Rejected because it makes our own quality bar cost the customer money and because it penalises duplex, the exact hardware we are selling to.

schemaChanges.change: New table: id uuid_v7 pk, org_id uuid not null, exam_id uuid not null, source_kind text check in ('pdf','tiff','images','escl','folder'), source_name text (display name only, never a filesystem path), source_digest bytea not null (sha256 of bytes), page_count int not null, pages_done int not null default 0, device_id text, operator_user_id uuid not null, status text check in ('running','paused','done','abandoned'), started_at timestamptz, finished_at timestamptz.
schemaChanges.why: A batch is a first class object because it can be paused, resumed, audited and attributed. operator_user_id is what makes the institution tier auditable: in a consumer org it is always the owner, in a school it answers 'who ran the grade 9 sitting'.

schemaChanges.change: create unique index uq_batches_digest on batches(org_id, exam_id, source_digest); create index idx_batches_org_exam on batches(org_id, exam_id).
schemaChanges.why: The digest unique index is the whole duplicate import defence: dropping the same PDF twice into the same exam is caught before a single paper is created, which is the batch scale version of PLAN section 4 rule 8.

schemaChanges.change: add column batch_id uuid null; add column source_page int null; add column source text not null default 'camera' check (source in ('camera','pdf','tiff','image','escl')).
