schemaChanges.why: source_page is the physical handle back to the paper stack and the only way a teacher can act on a failure. source default 'camera' means every existing row and the entire camera path are untouched by this migration.

schemaChanges.change: New table: batch_id uuid, page_no int, org_id uuid, outcome text check in ('graded','ambiguous','noSheet','geometryFailed','codeUnreadable','duplicate'), scan_id uuid null, reason_code text null (values: dpi_too_low, no_fiducials, skew_gt_12deg, code_crc_fail, mrc_compression, page_too_dark), rotation_applied smallint null, primary key (batch_id, page_no).
schemaChanges.why: This is the anti silent loss guarantee in schema form. One row per source page, so the completeness check is arithmetic rather than trust. Rows are tiny text and sync normally with the rest of the data.

schemaChanges.change: Product and CI invariant: for any batch with status='done', count(batch_pages where batch_id=b) must equal batches.page_count, and the count of rows with outcome in ('graded','ambiguous') must equal the number of scans with that batch_id.
schemaChanges.why: PLAN acceptance criterion 1 forbids silent errors and criterion 9 forbids silent duplicates. At batch scale the equivalent failure is a page that quietly vanishes among 600, and only an asserted invariant catches it.

schemaChanges.change: New local only table: batch_id uuid, page_no int, thumb blob (about 25 KB, 400x560 grayscale JPEG), name_crop blob, expires_at timestamptz not null default now() + interval '7 days'. Excluded from sync_queue by construction, and purged on batch close or on TTL.
schemaChanges.why: The bounded departure from PLAN section 7 described above. Isolating it in its own table, rather than adding a blob column to scans, is what makes 'never synced, always expiring' enforceable by inspection instead of by discipline.

schemaChanges.change: papers_graded increments only for batch_pages rows with outcome in ('graded','ambiguous'); no schema change, but the increment site moves behind a single function shared by the camera and batch paths.
schemaChanges.why: Duplex scanning of single sided sheets emits roughly two images per paper. Metering pages instead of papers would halve a school's purchased quota on exactly the hardware the tier is sold for.

schemaChanges.change: New table for the institution tier: org_id uuid, user_id uuid, month date, allocated int, primary key (org_id, user_id, month), plus orgs gains monthly_pool int and unallocated is derived as monthly_pool minus sum(allocated).
schemaChanges.why: The product owner asked for quota allocation between invited accounts. Keeping allocation per month mirrors the existing usage(org_id, month) key so the check is a single join, and keeping the pool on orgs means an unallocated remainder exists rather than the administrator having to distribute every last paper.

schemaChanges.table: templates, exams, answer_keys, students, scans, batches, batch_pages, org_quotas
schemaChanges.change: No change required to the org_id column that already exists on every table; new tables carry org_id and get the same deny by default RLS policy using (org_id = (select auth.jwt()->>'org_id')::uuid).
schemaChanges.why: PLAN section 5 put org_id everywhere from day one precisely so this tier costs no migration of the isolation model. The new tables must be added to the RLS integration test that attempts cross org reads, or the strongest guarantee in the project develops a hole at exactly the moment orgs stop being one teacher.

risks.risk: High compression / MRC PDF (Canon Compact PDF, Ricoh high compression PDF, JPXDecode or a bitonal mask over a low resolution background) recomposites page edges by a pixel or two and quietly degrades fill fraction, so the batch grades at 97% instead of 99.7% and nobody knows why.
risks.mitigation: Detect the filter and the layer structure at import, refuse or warn with the exact copier setting to change, and put one genuine compact PDF batch into the golden set so the regression is measured rather than assumed. Add a scanner arm to the golden set generally: three multi page PDFs from three device classes plus one deliberately broken batch containing a skewed feed, a missing page from a double feed, an upside down page and blank backs.

risks.risk: The desktop folder watch helper is the most underestimated line item in this design. It is a Windows binary plus a macOS binary, with code signing, notarisation, silent update and antivirus false positive handling, and it is also the prerequisite for eSCL discovery since a browser cannot do mDNS.
risks.mitigation: Ship v1 as drag and drop only, which needs no binary at all and already covers the copier drop folder if the operator opens it from the same PC. Schedule the helper as its own milestone with its own signing budget and treat eSCL as a v2 feature that rides on it, so the tier can be sold and used before any binary exists.

risks.risk: Double feeds produce a missing student rather than a wrong grade, and they are invisible to us: the file simply has 599 pages instead of 600. Sheetfed units such as the fi-8170 have ultrasonic double feed detection, but a copier DADF usually does not.
risks.mitigation: Roster completeness reconciliation after every batch: '27 of 30 students in class 3/A have a paper, missing Ahmad, Sara, Faisal'. This is only possible because CSV roster import is already in MVP scope, and it is the single strongest argument that bulk ingestion is an institution capability, since the value is the completeness workflow rather than the file parsing.

risks.risk: The preview retention change makes our currently published privacy wording false if the marketing page ships unchanged, which would be a worse breach of trust than the storage itself and is directly contrary to the discoverability strategy of publishing verifiable numbers.
risks.mitigation: Treat the privacy page edit as part of the same pull request as batch_page_previews, with the new sentence written in Arabic first, and expose a visible 'previews stored: 20, purge now' control in the batch screen so the claim and the product agree.

risks.risk: Throughput mismatch and backpressure. A fi-8170 at 70 ppm delivers about one page per second, and a 100 sheet hopper empties in 86 seconds, so a 600 page sitting is about 9 minutes of feeding. If grading runs at 400 to 600 ms per page on two mobile workers, the operator finishes feeding long before grading finishes, and a UI that implies live results will read as a hang.
risks.mitigation: Make the asynchrony explicit in the UI ('feeding complete, grading 412 of 600, about 2 minutes left') rather than hiding it, keep commits at one transaction per 50 papers so progress is durable, and make the batch resumable from pages_done so closing the laptop is not a lost hour.

risks.risk: eSCL discovery fails on real school networks, where printers commonly sit on a separate VLAN and mDNS is not forwarded between segments, so the Scan button finds nothing and looks broken.
risks.mitigation: Always offer manual IP or hostname entry alongside discovery, probe the standard eSCL endpoint directly, and keep the watched folder route as the supported default so eSCL is a convenience rather than the path the tier depends on.

result.rejected: The most tempting wrong answer is: accept an upload and grade it on the server. One endpoint, no browser compatibility matrix, no worker pool, no desktop helper, no memory budget, works from any phone and any old browser, and the file transport problem disappears entirely. It is genuinely the least code in this whole document, which is exactly why it will keep being proposed. It is wrong because it inverts the only durable advantage we have. PLAN section 9 puts a million users at 1,500 to 4,000 dollars a month precisely because the backend moves short text and never images or GPU work; a 300 to 500 MB colour batch per exam sitting turns that into a bandwidth and storage business against a market anchored at 26 riyals a year (COMPETITIVE-NOTES 57). It also converts a zero liability posture into a regulated one: under the Saudi PDPL, in force since September 2023 with a separate Regulations on Personal Data Transfers outside the Kingdom and SDAIA enforcement committees actively issuing decisions with power to suspend processing, uploading images of identifiable Saudi students' handwriting would demand KSA resident infrastructure, a data processing agreement with every school and a records of processing obligation, all of which a competitor can then point at while we can no longer say the one sentence that distinguishes us. A second, subtler version of the same mistake is to build the bulk importer only in the mobile app: that does not upload anything by itself, but since the file is on the PC beside the copier, it forces every user to move a large PDF through WhatsApp or Drive to reach their phone, and we would have caused the upload we refused to perform. The local browser plus local device design costs a worker pool and a signed helper, and it is the price of keeping the claim true. Sources verified for this analysis: Ricoh fi-8170 datasheet and product page (pfu-us.ricoh.com/scanners/fi/fi-8170), ScanSnap iX2500 and the discontinued iX1600 pages (pfu-us.ricoh.com/scanners/scansnap/ix2500 and /ix1600), Canon imageRUNNER ADVANCE DX C3835i product information (cla.canon.com and copiersonsale.com specifications), Mopria eSCL specification (mopria.org/mopria-escl-specification) with implementation detail from the Debian eSCL wiki and sane-airscan, pdfjs-dist release listing on npm, Android PDF rendering APIs including PdfRendererPreV (developer.android.com/media/grow/pdf-viewer), the absence of TIFF support in Android BitmapFactory, mupdf.js AGPL or commercial licensing (ArtifexSoftware/mupdf.js README), File System Access API support limited to Chromium with Firefox and Safari not implementing the local disk pickers (MDN showDirectoryPicker), and Saudi PDPL status and enforcement (iclg.com Data Protection 2026 Saudi Arabia chapter, dlapiperdataprotection.com).
